To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the minimal system that could be considered a self-maintaining autonomous system is one that is composed by a single cell, and (ii) the minimum number of molecules required for a single cell to be self-sufficient is around 1000.

the minimum requirements for the origin of a self-maintaining cellular system are the presence of a self-sustained chemical reaction, a membrane that can selectively allow the passage of certain molecules and a mechanism to maintain the system in a state of low entropy.
a self-sustaining cellular system must be able to: (a) exchange energy with its environment, and (b) exchange material with its environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a computer simulation of an autonomous system, capable of reproducing itself and of maintaining itself in a given environment.
the design of a simulation model of a self-maintaining cellular system.
the question: What are the minimal requirements for the emergence of an autonomous system?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the minimal requirements for a system to be considered alive are (a) a thermodynamic system that (b) is able to maintain a constant temperature and a constant volume, (c) that is able to self-maintain its own structure, (d) that is capable of self-replication, (e) and is able to self-organize its internal structure in a way that allows it to respond to environmental changes in an adaptive way.

a minimal self-maintaining system requires at least a minimal set of components (e.g. a membrane, a source of chemical energy, and a minimal set of chemical reactions), and an organizational structure (e.g. an internal compartment and a mechanism for the transport of molecules across the membrane).

the minimal requirements to produce a self-maintaining cellular system are: a) a membrane, b) an internal compartment, c) a source of free energy, d) a set of enzymes and a mechanism for the synthesis of new ones, e) a set of molecules to be used as building blocks and f) a set of molecular interactions that allow the formation of a self-replicating system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the origin of autonomous systems (i.e. life) is a consequence of the thermodynamic requirements of self-maintenance, the existence of chemical reactions that are capable of producing the necessary energy and the existence of chemical compounds with a high capacity for self-reproduction.

the minimal requirements for the origin of autonomous systems are: a) the existence of a source of energy, b) the presence of a material substrate (or medium), c) the existence of an information storage and processing system and d) a mechanism for the reproduction of the whole system.

a self-reproducing, self-maintaining and self-repairing system is a thermodynamic system that is able to maintain a stable internal structure (i.e. a homeostatic state) by means of a continuous flow of energy, materials, and information from its environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the minimal requirements to sustain a self-maintaining system are not only the ones related to thermodynamics, but they also involve the presence of a self-referential organization that is able to control the thermodynamic fluxes and to self-regulate the system.

a self-maintaining system must have a certain degree of complexity and a certain level of organization in order to maintain a constant energy flow through the system, which is a fundamental condition for its survival.
a minimal self-maintaining cellular system should be able to maintain a stable and constant temperature in its environment.
